analysis:
This batch is test-only. It covers four KVCacheSSD test files under provider-swift/Tests, and no production source was supplied.

What the tests imply about production behavior (T-041, the SSD tier's TTL, retirement and file-coordination posture):
(1) SSDHybridCheckpointCoordinationTests.swift head:21-87. Concurrent same-file readers now share a read lease and no longer queue. Only a reader holding the file alone refreshes its mtime. A receipt made stale by that refresh forces reauthentication (donationReadBytes>0).
(2) head:128-168. A queued writer goes ahead of readers that arrive later, which prevents writer starvation.
(3) head:170-238. Retirement, eviction and scans skip a file another reader holds. A corrupt file is removed only by a reader holding it alone.
(4) SSDHybridCheckpointRecencyTests.swift head:83-117. recencyRefreshSeconds=60 limits mtime rewrites to one per interval; the in-memory index still records every hit.
(5) head:119-180. Whole-root TTL maintenance keeps a file whose in-memory lastAccess is newer than the cutoff and persists that mtime. The sweep then expires the file one TTL after the last hit, so the sliding TTL stays bounded at 30 minutes.
(6) SSDOwnedEntryRetirementTests.swift head:36-66. A new unusedSince cutoff spares entries hit after the cutoff, never moves an mtime backward, and leaves unconditional retirement in place for budget eviction.
(7) SSDShorterCheckpointRestoreTests.swift (metadata only; ranges at head 307-348) adjusts a same-ID replacement test for the shared lease.

Security relevance: the persisted mtime may lag the true last hit by up to 60s, or longer when reads overlap. The tests show the in-memory index is consulted at sweep and retirement, so expiry still tracks the last hit and does not extend beyond TTL. Receipt and file-identity checks still reauthenticate after an mtime change. No crypto, naming, salt or epoch change is visible, and the tests assert the epoch is unchanged.

No regression can be established from tests alone.

Open questions for integration, which need the production SSDHybridCheckpointStore, SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator, SSDWholeRootMaintainer and SSDOwnedEntryRetirement source:
- Whether a lone reader's TTL is checked under the lease before I/O. The queuedValidity test at head:279-319 suggests it is.
- Whether the shared-read lease can starve retirement or TTL deletion indefinitely under continuous overlapping reads. That would extend at-rest retention beyond the 30-minute TTL (T-041(b)); production code is needed to confirm writer and retirement precedence.
- Whether whole-root maintenance's use of in-memory recency can be inflated by adversarial same-account traffic beyond the normal sliding behavior.
